noble.text: You’re accustomed to a world where words, decisions, and the people you know can carry considerable influence. The Force may give you a different understanding of that influence. What would you like to learn about it?
noble.speaker: mentor

scoundrel.text: I imagine you’ve learned to rely on your instincts, particularly when things don’t go as expected. That experience needn’t be forgotten here. Tell me, what interests you about learning the ways of the Jedi?
scoundrel.speaker: mentor

scout.text: You’ve learned to observe your surroundings and recognize things that others might overlook. Those are valuable habits, especially when learning to sense the Force. What would you like to explore first?
scout.speaker: mentor

soldier.text: Your training has taught you discipline and how to act when circumstances become dangerous. Those lessons will serve you here as well, though you may find that the Force asks something different of you. What are you hoping to learn?
soldier.speaker: mentor

q2.text: You haven't come here empty-handed. Everything you've learned before still has its place, and these lessons may give you new ways to use it. How do you hope they'll fit together?
q2.speaker: mentor

q3.text: Some students come looking for a few useful lessons. Others discover they want to keep learning for years. You don't need to decide forever, but how far would you like to pursue this?
q3.speaker: mentor

q4.text: Let's try something. I'd like you to consider a situation and tell me how you would approach it. Take a moment to think before answering.
q4.speaker: mentor

q5.text: You don't need to know everything you'll eventually become. For now, think about what's ahead of you. What's something you hope these lessons will help you accomplish?
q5.speaker: mentor

jedi.text: Observation: Your Jedi studies have given you a different perspective on the decisions people make, Master. Noble training offers ways to bring people together and put those decisions into motion. Which abilities would you most like to develop?
jedi.speaker: mentor

scoundrel.text: Observation: Your previous training may have taught you to improvise when circumstances turn against you, Master. I can also help you shape those circumstances beforehand. Which of these skills interests you?
scoundrel.speaker: mentor

scout.text: Assessment: Learning to recognize what others overlook is useful, Master. Learning how to act upon that information through planning, negotiation, or leadership can be equally valuable. What would you like to cultivate?
scout.speaker: mentor

soldier.text: Observation: Your martial training offers ways to face a threat directly, Master. Noble instruction can also help you organize allies, manage resources, and resolve disputes before they become battles. Which capability would you prefer to explore?
soldier.speaker: mentor

q2.text: Assessment: Your previous training is an asset, Master, not something to be discarded. We can add the skills to coordinate people, resources, and information around what you already do well. How would you like these capabilities to work together?
q2.speaker: mentor

q3.text: Planning Inquiry: A brief course of study may serve one purpose; sustained training may serve another. Neither is inherently superior, Master. How much of your time would you like to devote to this discipline?
q3.speaker: mentor

q4.text: Hypothetical Scenario: A complication now requires your judgment, Master. I recommend considering both the information and the resources available to you. How would you proceed?
q4.speaker: mentor

q5.text: Long-Term Projection: I can outline several promising avenues, Master, but I would prefer to begin with a goal that matters to you. What would you like your next step to accomplish?
q5.speaker: mentor

jedi.text: So ye've studied the Jedi way, eh? A steady head'll serve ye well out here, matey. Now let's see what quick thinking, clever talk, and a few less respectable tricks can add. What catches yer fancy?
jedi.speaker: mentor

noble.text: Ye've learned there's power in knowin' how to deal with people, matey. Out beyond the fancy ports, it also pays to know how to slip past trouble when talk won't do. What trick would ye like to pick up?
noble.speaker: mentor

scout.text: Know how to find yer way through rough country, do ye? Good! But a locked hatch or a crooked deal can be just as dangerous as a wild beast. What would ye like ol' Salty to teach ye?
scout.speaker: mentor

soldier.text: Know yer way around a fight, eh? Handy skill, matey. But a fast getaway or a well-timed bluff can save ye a heap o' ammunition. Which new trick interests ye?
soldier.speaker: mentor

q2.text: Ye've already got a few tricks aboard, matey. I'm not here to toss 'em overboard. What would ye like to add to yer kit, and how'll ye use it alongside what ye know?
q2.speaker: mentor

q3.text: Some folk learn one good trick and sail on. Others stay till they know every rope aboard. Maybe ye haven't decided yet. How deep are ye plannin' to go, matey?
q3.speaker: mentor

q4.text: Right, matey, here's a scrape worth thinkin' about. Might be more than one way through it. How would ye play it?
q4.speaker: mentor

q5.text: Can't chart the whole galaxy in one jump, matey. Pick the next port worth reachin'. What d'ye want this training to help ye pull off?
q5.speaker: mentor

jedi.text: Jedi training gives you a few advantages most people don’t have. Doesn’t mean you can’t benefit from knowing how to work without them. So, what are you looking to learn?
jedi.speaker: mentor

noble.text: You’re probably accustomed to getting information out of people. Useful skill. Out here, though, there’s plenty of information that nobody’s going to volunteer. What would you like to get better at finding for yourself?
noble.speaker: mentor

scoundrel.text: You’re used to thinking on your feet. Good. I’d like to see what you can do when you’ve got time to prepare instead. What skills are you interested in developing?
scoundrel.speaker: mentor

soldier.text: You already know how to handle yourself in a fight. That’s useful, but sometimes the best fight is the one you see coming early enough to avoid. What would you like to work on?
soldier.speaker: mentor

q2.text: You've already got experience, so we're not starting from scratch. Think about what you do well and what you'd like to do differently. Where do you want this training to help?
q2.speaker: mentor

q3.text: I can teach you a few useful things, or we can put some real time into this. Maybe you don't know yet. How much are you planning to commit to your training?
q3.speaker: mentor

q4.text: All right, here's one to think through. Pay attention to what you know, what you don't, and what you have available. What would you do?
q4.speaker: mentor

q5.text: Big ambitions are fine, but we should start with something you can actually work toward. What's your next objective, and how do you see this training helping you reach it?
q5.speaker: mentor

jedi.text: Ah, a Jedi! You’ve got those lightsabers and the Force and all that. Pretty useful! But there’s plenty more to fighting than swinging one of those things around. What do you want to learn?
jedi.speaker: mentor

noble.text: So, you’re used to talking your way through trouble, eh? Good skill to have. But if somebody decides to stop listening, it’s nice to have another option! What do you want to get better at?
noble.speaker: mentor

scoundrel.text: Ha! I like someone who knows how to get out of trouble. Though I suppose learning to stand your ground wouldn’t hurt either. What do you want me to teach you?
scoundrel.speaker: mentor

scout.text: Scouting, eh? So you’re good at finding trouble before it finds you. That’s useful! Now, what would you like to learn about dealing with it?
scout.speaker: mentor

q2.text: You've got some experience already. Good! We can build on that, patch up what isn't working, or try something new. What sounds useful to you?
q2.speaker: mentor

q3.text: Nothing wrong with learning a little, and nothing wrong with wanting to learn everything! You don't have to make up your mind today, either. How far do you think you'll take this?
q3.speaker: mentor

q4.text: All right, here's a problem for you. Don't worry about giving me the answer you think I want. Tell me how you'd handle it!
q4.speaker: mentor

q5.text: Good! Now tell me what you want to do with all this. Doesn't have to be some grand, heroic thing. Just something worth working toward. What's next for you?
q5.speaker: mentor

methods.text: I would speak with each leader separately to learn what they actually fear losing.
